original_question: Let St be a Steiner tree in Euclidean space, let A be its terminal set, and fix x and r > 0 so that Br(x) contains no terminal points, that is, A ∩ Br(x) = ∅. Assume moreover that the tree has finite length inside Br(x). For t = 1/2, or more generally for t ∈ (0, 1), what is the largest possible number of intersection points between the tree and the sphere ∂Btr(x)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.3, Question 2.5 ("Density type questions"), together with the setup immediately preceding it and the remark immediately following it.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the object as a Steiner tree in Euclidean space, introduces the terminal set A, imposes the local no-terminal condition A ∩ B_r(x) = ∅, includes the paper’s local finiteness hypothesis inside the ball, and asks for the maximal number of intersection points with a concentric sphere, with special attention to the half-radius case t = 1/2.
missing_details: The exact target in the paper is Question 2.5 in Section 2.3, not Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3; your draft clearly points to the later Steiner-tree section on density-type questions.
The local finiteness assumption should be stated in the paper’s measure-theoretic form as H^1(St ∩ B_r(x)) < ∞.

The paper’s official formulation centers the question on the half-radius sphere ∂B_{r/2}(x); the extension to other radii is only mentioned as a nearby variant ('or other t'), so t = 1/2 should remain the primary formulation.

The paper frames these questions for Steiner trees in Euclidean spaces generally, but the nearby discussion singles out the planar case as the first nontrivial open instance; the draft does not explicitly flag that planar emphasis.

The nearby context notes that in the planar case the local finiteness condition can be replaced by x not belonging to the closure of the terminal set; this paper-specific refinement is omitted in the draft.

The paper also notes optional extra restrictions one may impose, such as requiring St ∩ B_r(x) to be connected or full; these are not part of the main question, but they are part of the nearby scope-setting context.
The nearby discussion records a planar example with 6 points on the half-radius circle and states that it is open whether 6 is optimal in the plane; this sharpens the intended focus of the question.
refined_question: Let St ⊂ ℝ^d be a Steiner tree with terminal set A. Fix x ∈ ℝ^d and r > 0 such that A ∩ B_r(x) = ∅, and assume the local length is finite in the sense that H^1(St ∩ B_r(x)) < ∞. What is the maximal possible cardinality of St ∩ ∂B_{r/2}(x)? More generally, for a fixed t ∈ (0,1), what is the maximal possible cardinality of St ∩ ∂B_{tr}(x)?
justification: The draft unmistakably targets the Steiner-tree 'density type questions' subsection, where the paper first sets up exactly the same local hypotheses: a Steiner tree St, a ball B_r(x) containing no terminal points, and a local finiteness assumption on St inside that ball. The very next item is Question 2.5, which asks for the largest possible number of intersection points with the concentric sphere at half radius, while also indicating a variant for other values of t. The follow-up sentence gives a planar example with 6 such points and says it is open whether this is maximal in the plane. So the right refinement is not a broader Steiner-tree regularity problem, but precisely this local intersection-count question in the form above.
